response.sql: WITH cat AS (SELECT category, AVG(remaining) AS avg_remaining, SUM(amount - spent) AS total FROM budget WHERE amount >= 75 GROUP BY category), overall AS (SELECT AVG(total) AS overall_avg FROM cat) SELECT cat.category, cat.avg_remaining, cat.total, cat.total - overall.overall_avg AS above_overall_avg FROM cat CROSS JOIN overall WHERE cat.total > overall.overall_avg;

assumptions.assumption: Only budget rows with amount >= 75 are used; rows with NULL amount are excluded by that filter.

Missing values are skipped per aggregate: AVG(remaining) ignores NULL remaining, and SUM(amount - spent) drops any row whose spent is NULL (its amount is not counted). A category whose values are all missing gets a NULL average or total.
Budget rows with a NULL category form their own group under GROUP BY rather than being excluded.
The overall average is the mean of the per-category totals, skipping NULL totals. If no category has a non-NULL total, the average is NULL and no rows are returned.

alternatives.interpretation: Compute each category's total as SUM(amount) - SUM(spent), so a row with a missing spent still contributes its full amount to the total instead of being dropped.
